Interview Experience
Summer Internship 2023
Sachit A. Sankhe
TY B.Tech IT 2020-24
Eligibility:-
●Open to all branches.
●No CGPA criteria
About the Internship offer:-
●2-month Internship
●25000/- Rs per month
About the company:-
Think360 partners with clients at the intersection of data algorithms, technology, and
business – to solve their most complex problems. Meaning the company helps
businesses or clients to solve their problems using Data Analytics and Artificial
Intelligence.

Two roles were offered:-
●
Python Developer
●
Data analyst
I got selected for the Python Developer role, so will be talking about my Interview
experience for the python developer position.
First, there was an Online test, then 2 rounds of interviews.
Online test:-
The test was scheduled for 19th November. The test was unique in the
way that the test links were forwarded to us at 2 pm and we were given time until
EOD, so we could give the test any time between 2 to EOD. This was because
the platform on which the Online Test was scheduled allowed only a certain
number of students to give the test at a time(i guess 10 students at once). So I
gave the test at 9 pm so that there is no such problem.
The platform was CoderByte. Never used it before. The test duration was 2
hours for the python developer test and 1hr 30 min for the data analyst role.
The test had 3 problems, 2 DSA questions, and 1 SQL question.
Q1) Smallest window in a string containing all the
characters of another string | Practice |
GeeksforGeeks
The problem was medium or I can say common. The unique thing in this
assessment is that there will be a unique string given to you that will be unique to

your account only. You have to replace all the characters in your Output string
that appear in the unique string with –[that_character]--
I know that you didn’t understand. I’ll give an example
If 2 strings given to you are strArr =  ["aabdccdbcacd", "aad"] then the smallest
substring of strArr[0] that contains all of the characters in strArr[1] is "aabd".
And let’s say the unique string given to you is ao139dc4.
Then since your output i.e (aabd) contains a,d that is also present in the
unique string. So you have to output the answer as –a—-a–b–d–
(double dash then the character then again double dash)
Another example(same unique string)
Q2 ) LRU Cache | Practice | GeeksforGeeks
Again a medium question but a common question. The same pattern
followed in this question as well. The same unique string will be used to
modify the output and give the answer.
Q3) One table was given (Column were FirstName,
LastName, and Age).

The query was to return the rows where Lastname = Musk or FirstName
= Jeff & had to order_by age.
It was a simple query.
The questions had different numbers of points with the Q2 having most
points and Q3 having the least points. Don’t remember the exact points.
I solved 2 & the 3rd problem completely and 8 test cases for the first
problem. The main thing was that I took a lot of time to understand the
unique string pattern point as the language was complicated. As a result, I
wasn't able to code it out properly.
We received the Shortlisted Candidates list on 21 November with 16
candidates for the python developer role and 14 candidates for data
analyst.
Interviews were conducted online. Our interviews were scheduled for 22nd
November. Everyone was allocated 30 mins with rounds starting from
around 10:30 am & last round around 3:30 pm. But due to some practical or
viva of the CS branch, the interviews were postponed.
My interview that was to be conducted at 1:30 pm was conducted at 4 pm.

Round 1 of Interview:-
The interviewer first asked me to introduce myself. I prepared my
Introduction such that I can tell the interviewer about the projects or work
that I had done in python. (Since it was a python developer role).
The introduction is one of the most important pieces of preparation as you
can easily steer the interview into the zone where you are confident and can
put a good impression on the interviewer.
After that Interviewer asked about my Online Judge Project and what was it
about in very brief. I explained to him about it and then we moved on to the
python specific questions.
The interviewer asked different questions based on differences between
python and java or c++. Also how to declare private variables and protected
variable in python. How do classes work, how to declare objects, what are
decorators, what is a module, what is pip, and what is a virtual environment
etc. I had prepared for this question from Top Python Interview Questions
(2023) - InterviewBit also from GFG as well.
The main crux is that tell them about the instances of where you have used
the specific concept or feature. This will show the interviewer that you don’t
only have theoretical knowledge but also practical knowledge. And I believe
that was something that gave me an edge over others. I wasn’t able to
answer all the questions but the topics that I knew, I explained them
properly and with a real-life use case or any instance where I used it.
Also, prepare for OOPS in python.

The interview lasted for about 30-35 minutes.
Since the last interview was completed by 5:30 pm. So Round 2 was
scheduled the next day and around 5 to 6 students were selected for Round
2.
The result for the data analyst role was announced on 22 November i.e
same day. And some interviews for Round 2 were completed that day itself.
Round 2 of Interview:
My interview was scheduled for 1 pm. The interviewer asked me to
introduce myself and simultaneously told me to share the screen. I thought
that this would be an HR interview or an Interview based on projects but
this was a complete DSA interview.
The interviewer told me to open a notepad and sent a question on the
google meet chat. The question was Row with max 1s | Practice |
GeeksforGeeks.
I had not solved this question but had looked at another similar one. So I
started with the most basic brute force approach. And then progressively
improved my approach to binary search. (Also, keep on asking clarifying
questions as One of the questions I asked that whether the columns are
sorted or not also is there a chance that a row contains zero number of 1s.)
After that, the interviewer asked me to roughly code the binary function for
solving the question. I had missed one thing but with a hint, I was able to

code a proper solution. After that, he asked if I could come up with an
O(n) approach.
I was unable to find one, so then we moved on to the next question.
The next question was Sort an array of 0s, 1s and 2s | Dutch National Flag
problem - GeeksforGeeks. Had solved a similar problem, I started with the
same brute force and then spent some time thinking if it could be solved
with only two pointers, but then with some hints, I was able to code a
proper solution to the problem. He asked me to code the problem and
execute the code. I did that properly while continuously thinking out loud
about how I was thinking and coding it.
After 5 days, TPO sent the mail and I was the only one selected for the
python role.
This was my interview experience for the Intern role.
